forecasts.question: Will AGI be developed before 1 January 2030?
forecasts.key_change: No major movement. Davos 2026 commentary continues to show Amodei bullish (~2027) and Hassabis at ~50% by 2030. No formal AGI claim by a lab; Gemini 3.5 Pro pending public release in June 2026 but not pitched as AGI.
forecasts.base_rate: Resolution requires a credible lab announcement OR 3+ leading researchers calling it. Reference class: prior 'AI breakthrough' resolutions tend to come well after sustained internal capability rather than abruptly; ~3.5 yrs remaining.

factors_up.factor: Continued bullish lab leadership statements (Amodei) and AI-automating-AI feedback loops
Major frontier model releases (Gemini 3.5 Pro, OpenAI, Anthropic) compressing timelines

factors_down.factor: No public AGI claim from any major lab; Hassabis still cautious
Definitional ambiguity — what counts as AGI is contested, raising the bar for the '3+ researchers' clause
Resolution requires public announcement, not just internal capability

key_uncertainties: Whether internal lab progress translates to public AGI declarations before 2030
Whether definitional disputes will deter labs from making formal claims
Pace of self-improvement loops in 2027-2029
update_triggers: Formal AGI claim from a frontier lab
Public statement by 2+ senior researchers at OpenAI/Anthropic/DeepMind that AGI is achieved
METR/eval benchmark crossing AGI-relevant threshold

forecasts.question: Will economic consultancy lose ≥33% value/jobs by end 2030 due to AI?
forecasts.key_change: Slight downward drift. McKinsey ~10% cuts and broad Big-3 restructuring continue, but BCG is actually growing revenue via AI ($3.6B of $14.4B from AI work). Headline picture is a mix shift, not a 33% decline.
forecasts.base_rate: Sector-wide ≥33% revenue or employment decline within ~4-5 years is rare; typically requires depression or structural collapse. Recent AI-led restructurings are mostly mid-single-digit to ~10% headcount.

factors_up.factor: McKinsey/BCG/Bain/Deloitte all running AI-driven layoffs in entry-level roles
40% productivity gains reported by Forrester reduce junior headcount needs
Client procurement teams squeezing fees as AI exposes effort costs

factors_down.factor: BCG growing revenue rapidly from AI advisory — partially offsets disintermediation
33% is a very high bar; current trajectory is closer to 10-15% headcount
Resolution requires 2+ credible analyses attributing decline primarily to AI

key_uncertainties: Whether firms succeed in pivoting to AI advisory faster than commodity work erodes
Whether '≥33% decline' will manifest in revenue, headcount, or neither at the aggregate level
How attribution disputes will play out in 2+ credible analyses
update_triggers: Big-3 quarterly results showing >20% revenue decline
ONS/BLS data showing >20% drop in management consultancy employment
Sector report from BIS/McKinsey itself confirming AI-driven structural decline

forecasts.question: Will Labour be largest party at next UK General Election?
forecasts.key_change: No change. June 2026 PollCheck average: Reform 27.3%, Labour 19.0%, Con 18.3%. Electoral Calculus April MRP gave Reform 188 seats, Labour just 86. Labour would need a ~10pt swing back across ~3 years.
forecasts.base_rate: Governing parties whose poll share collapses ~25pts mid-term historically recover only modestly; falling from 1st to 3rd in seat projections rarely reverses to 1st within 3 years.

factors_up.factor: Election not until end 2029 — ~3.5 years for Labour to recover
Reform support could fragment if it enters coalition or faces party-management issues
UK FPTP could split right-wing vote between Reform + Con, benefiting Labour in seats

factors_down.factor: Labour trailing both Reform AND Con in vote share consistently
Government approval at historic lows similar to previous government's worst
MRP modelling shows Labour at ~86 seats — structurally adverse map

key_uncertainties: Whether Reform consolidates the right or splits the right-wing vote at the GE
Whether Labour can stage a mid-term recovery
Boundary changes and tactical voting dynamics
update_triggers: Labour poll lead returning
Reform formal pact or merger with Conservatives
By-election results showing Labour recovery

forecasts.question: Will AGI be developed before 1 January 2035?
forecasts.key_change: No change. Most lab leaders' median estimates fall within the 2027-2032 window; 9 years is enough time to bridge definitional disputes and force public claims. Strong consensus among Amodei/Hassabis/Altman that AGI is plausible by early 2030s.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: 9-year windows for transformative tech rarely close without occurrence when active credible R&D programmes exist; AGI prediction markets cluster median ~2030.

factors_up.factor: Multiple frontier labs racing with billions in capex
Capability scaling continues unabated; agent benchmarks compounding
9 years is long horizon — even moderate compounding suffices

factors_down.factor: Definitional disputes may persist past 2035
Compute/energy bottlenecks could slow scaling
Regulatory shock or AI winter unlikely but non-zero

key_uncertainties: Whether scaling laws hold to 2030+
How resolution will be operationalised by markets/researchers
Risk of significant slowdown from regulation or geopolitics
update_triggers: Public AGI claim from frontier lab
Major capability discontinuity (recursive self-improvement)
Regulatory moratorium on frontier training runs

forecasts.question: Will China initiate a military blockade or invasion of Taiwan before 1 January 2030?
forecasts.key_change: No change. PLA grey-zone activity continues but ASPI and US State Dept assessments view 2026 not the year for blockade/invasion. Taiwan passed $25B defence supplement. PRC strategy remains coercion-short-of-war.
forecasts.base_rate: Historical base rate of major-power amphibious assault or formal blockade against a peer adjacent state in any given ~3.5yr period: low single digits.

factors_up.factor: PLA accelerating capability build, joint exercises, drone incursions
Perceived window of US distraction (Middle East deployments)
Xi's stated 2027 PLA readiness deadline

factors_down.factor: Expert consensus that PRC prefers coercion to direct conflict
Costs/risks for Xi remain extreme; semiconductor dependence runs both ways
Taiwan defence buildup and US Indo-Pacific posture deter timing

key_uncertainties: Xi's personal risk tolerance and succession dynamics
Severity of US-China decoupling shocks
Possible Taiwan independence declaration triggering response
update_triggers: PLA conducting exercises that don't conclude (transition to blockade)
Major escalation in Taiwan Strait crossings
Xi statement explicitly committing to military action

forecasts.question: Will UK annual CPI inflation fall below 2.0% for at least one month before 1 January 2027?
forecasts.key_change: Slight upward revision. April 2026 CPI came in at 2.8% (down from 3.3% in March) thanks to energy price cap. Core 2.5%, services 3.2%. Trajectory has surprised downward but reaching <2.0% in just 7-8 months requires another significant moderation.
forecasts.base_rate: From 2.8% in April 2026, reaching <2.0% within ~7 monthly prints is possible only with sustained energy moderation and services disinflation. Most forecaster averages have UK inflation hovering 2.2-2.5% through 2026.

factors_up.factor: April print surprised significantly to downside
Energy price cap effects could continue working through
Services inflation lowest since Jan 2022 — disinflation broadening

factors_down.factor: Still 0.8pp gap to close in 7 monthly prints
Wage growth and services stickiness above 3%
Treasury survey average forecasts 0.9% GDP/sticky inflation environment

key_uncertainties: Pace of services disinflation in summer/autumn 2026
Energy market volatility from Middle East conflict
Pass-through of wage settlements
update_triggers: Next ONS print significantly below 2.5%
BoE signalling that <2% is being reached
Energy price shock reversing the trajectory

forecasts.question: Will Spider-Man: Brand New Day gross over $1.5B worldwide by 31 December 2026?
forecasts.key_change: Downward revision. Closer inspection of base rates: only one solo Spider-Man (No Way Home, $1.92B) has cleared $1.5B; tracking suggests $1B+ as base case. Polymarket gives 54.5% prob of being top domestic film of 2026 (not the same as $1.5B WW). Release is July 31, leaving ~5 months for theatrical run.
forecasts.base_rate: Of 8 solo live-action Spider-Man films, 1 grossed >$1.5B WW (12.5%). Conditional on extreme anticipation, MCU return, and Day/Holland reunion, base rate jumps; still <80%.

factors_up.factor: Massive anticipation; 4-year gap since No Way Home
Polymarket implies high domestic strength; multiplier likely strong
July 31 release gives 5 months of theatrical runway

factors_down.factor: Only No Way Home has crossed $1.5B solo; $1.5B is a stretch threshold
MCU brand fatigue post-2023 has dragged subsequent releases
China and international markets weaker for Marvel post-2022

key_uncertainties: Opening weekend reception and word of mouth
International (especially China) performance
Competition from late-2026 releases
update_triggers: Opening weekend numbers
Tracking estimates updated 2-3 weeks pre-release
Box Office Mojo reporting milestone passes

forecasts.question: Will OpenAI and Anthropic have a combined ARR exceeding $70B by 31 December 2026?
forecasts.key_change: Essentially resolved. Anthropic ~$45B ARR, OpenAI ~$33B ARR per May 2026 reporting = ~$78B already, even accepting OpenAI's contested ~$22B Anthropic figure ($55B combined). Resolution requires Q4 2026 reporting, so the only risk is an unprecedented collapse.
forecasts.base_rate: Companies sustaining >$60B combined ARR rarely collapse below that in 6 months absent catastrophic event.

factors_up.factor: Already exceeding $70B per current reporting
Both firms accelerating enterprise contracts
Q4 2026 is the resolution window; revenue typically grows

factors_down.factor: OpenAI's accounting dispute could lower the combined headline
Tail-risk: major outage / governance crisis / regulatory action

key_uncertainties: Whether 'most recent credible reporting' will use consistent ARR definitions
Whether revenue/ARR distinction materially affects resolution
update_triggers: Reported ARR drop >$15B at either firm
Major governance/legal action affecting revenue recognition

forecasts.question: Will UK average annual real GDP growth exceed 1.5% across the 2030s (2030-2039)?
forecasts.key_change: Small downward drift. OBR March 2026 forecasts 1.1% p.p. growth and 1% productivity assumption; labour supply growth dropping to 0.5% by 2030. Headline GDP growth would sit ~1.4-1.6% on those assumptions — right at the threshold. Treasury independent forecaster average is more pessimistic (0.9-1.1%).
forecasts.base_rate: Decadal average for UK real GDP growth post-GFC: ~1.4% (2010s). Trend deterioration in productivity and demographics suggests slight downward pressure.

factors_up.factor: Possible AI-led productivity surge could lift trend growth
Investment recovery from depressed base
Planning reform / housing build-out potential upside

factors_down.factor: OBR baseline implies growth ~at or below 1.5% threshold
Labour supply growth declining to 0.5% by 2030
Fiscal headroom constrained; debt at 95% GDP

key_uncertainties: Scale of AI/productivity impact on UK economy specifically
Migration policy effects on labour supply
External shocks during the decade
update_triggers: OBR upward revision of medium-term potential growth
ONS productivity data showing sustained pick-up
Major policy shift (tax/planning/investment)
